1. **Inventory & assessment (T-14 days):** Document schema, extensions, roles, sequences, triggers, and total size (2 TB) of the on-prem PostgreSQL instance. Choose the migration method (e.g., `pg_dump`/`pg_restore` or logical replication via AWS DMS/GCP DMS/pglogical) based on downtime tolerance, and provision the target managed instance sized to match or exceed source capacity.

2. **Provision & configure target (T-10 days):** Stand up the managed cloud PostgreSQL instance, match version/extensions/parameters, configure networking (VPN/private link), security groups, and IAM/user roles. Enable automated backups on the new instance.

3. **Stakeholder communication #1 (T-7 days):** Notify all 4,000 DAU and internal stakeholders of the planned Sunday maintenance window, expected duration (2 hours), and fallback contact/status page, via email and in-app banner.

4. **Dry run / rehearsal on staging (T-5 days):** Take a full backup/snapshot of production, restore it into a non-production staging environment mirroring the target cloud service, and perform a complete rehearsal of the migration procedure (initial load + replication or dump/restore) end-to-end, timing each phase against the 2-hour window.

5. **Rehearsal verification & timing analysis (T-4 days):** On the staging copy, verify data integrity (row counts, checksums via `pg_checksums`/`md5` aggregates per table) and validate application connectivity/queries. Adjust the runbook and go/no-go criteria based on measured timings; escalate if rehearsal exceeds window with buffer.

6. **Final backup before cutover (Sunday, T-0, start of window):** Take a full, verified backup/snapshot of the production database (immediately before any destructive/modifying action) and confirm it is restorable; record backup ID/checksum for rollback reference.

7. **Enable maintenance mode & freeze writes:** Put the application into read-only/maintenance mode, notify stakeholders that the window has begun, and stop all write traffic to the on-prem database.

8. **Final data sync to cloud target:** Perform final incremental sync/replication catch-up (or final `pg_dump`/`pg_restore` if not using CDC) from on-prem to the managed cloud instance so it is byte-for-byte current with the frozen source.

9. **Post-migration integrity verification:** Run row-count comparisons, checksum/hash comparisons per table (e.g., `pg_dump --schema-only` diff plus data checksums), sequence value checks, and index/constraint validation between source and target before allowing writes.

10. **Cutover & smoke test:** Repoint application connection strings/DNS to the managed cloud database, run smoke tests (critical read/write transactions, key reports), and exit maintenance mode only if smoke tests and integrity checks pass.

11. **Rollback procedure (conditional, only if verification/smoke tests fail):** Repoint application back to the untouched on-prem primary (which was frozen but not altered), restore from the pre-cutover backup taken in Step 6 if any corruption occurred, and communicate the rollback and revised timeline to stakeholders; investigate failure before rescheduling.

12. **Post-migration communication & monitoring (T+0 to T+2 days):** Notify stakeholders of successful completion (or rollback) and window closure, then actively monitor performance, error rates, and replication/backup jobs on the new managed instance for 48 hours before decommissioning the on-prem server.
